pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/ue5-bridge/build/route.ts:47 This route is the backend of the agent tool pof_ue_build (tools/pof-mcp/src/tools/ue.ts:276 posts here). It parses any POST body into a UBT spawn with no token and no origin check, and no middleware/proxy exists in the repo to add one. So the stdio tool server's capability is also served by an unauthenticated localhost HTTP door that any browser tab can drive with a text/plain simple request: the local-port trap.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/ue5-bridge/build/route.ts:47 The agent-tool backend sits on a local HTTP listener with no origin validation or token. The standard: a local listener must validate origin or require a token.

src/app/api/pof-bridge/status/route.ts:26 An unreachable bridge used to return apiSuccess({connected:false}). It now returns the failure envelope with a kind (unreachable/timeout/malformed), so a failed call can no longer read as a success.
src/app/api/ue5-bridge/query/route.ts:90 Every editor action against the single-seat UE editor names an explicit object path. No argument refers to the current selection or the active level.

The pof_crash_analyze tool lives in tools/pof-mcp and reads /api/crash-analyzer, both outside this context.

pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: src/lib/claude-terminal/mcp-config.ts:17 The shell renders the Claude CLI's stream-json events (tool_use/tool_result for built-in Edit/Write/Read). It never configures, lists or calls MCP servers; the --mcp-config opt-in lives only in autonomous routes. A case-insensitive search of src/components/cli for mcp, inputSchema, tools/call and jsonrpc found nothing. Its tool-event handling belongs to the agent-cli-transport subject, not this one.
